grade.rationale: The file defines concise, immutable API contracts with clear nullability and no evident compilation issues. Its main weakness is that the mutation request represents constrained domain input as unrestricted strings, allowing invalid states unless every entry point performs separate validation.

summary: The response models are straightforward and maintainable. Strengthen the mutation boundary by validating or constraining Action and Pattern; test coverage remains unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied.

grade.rationale: The record shapes are internally coherent, but ScopeRuleMutationRequest permits unsupported actions and unusable patterns.
Immutable positional records are compact and easy to evolve, although a free-form Action duplicates the rule-action vocabulary across consumers and validators.
Names and nullability communicate the contracts well; the meaning and permitted values of Action are not encoded by the type.
The request type supplies no intrinsic validation signal for unsupported actions or blank patterns, leaving consistent rejection dependent on external code.
The immutable, value-comparable records are easy to instantiate and assert against. Coverage is unknown, not assumed absent.

findings.title: Mutation requests admit invalid action and pattern values
findings.description: Action and Pattern are unrestricted strings, so callers can construct requests containing an unsupported or misspelled action, an empty action, or a blank pattern. Nullable annotations do not enforce non-null or non-blank values at runtime, particularly at an HTTP deserialization boundary. Unless identical validation is applied at every consumer, invalid states can reach rule-processing logic and produce inconsistent failures.
findings.recommendation: Define the supported action vocabulary with a validated enum or domain value type, and enforce non-null, non-whitespace pattern validation at the request boundary. If wire compatibility requires strings, add explicit request validation that returns a clear client error and centralize it so all mutation paths use the same rules.
